[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] # Systematic Debugging
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] ## Overview
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] **Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] **Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] ## The Iron Law
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] ```
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] ```
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] ## When to Use
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] Use for ANY technical issue:
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - Test failures
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - Bugs in production
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - Unexpected behavior
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - Performance problems
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - Build failures
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - Integration issues
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] **Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - You've already tried multiple fixes
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - Previous fix didn't work
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - You don't fully understand the issue
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] **Don't skip when:**
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] - Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] ## The Four Phases
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] ### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] **BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - Don't skip past errors or warnings
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - They often contain the exact solution
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - Read stack traces completely
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 2. **Reproduce Consistently**
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - Can you trigger it reliably?
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - What are the exact steps?
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - Does it happen every time?
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 3. **Check Recent Changes**
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - What changed that could cause this?
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - Git diff, recent commits
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - New dependencies, config changes
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    - Environmental differences
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-09-02T08:00:52.010Z] [STDERR]    **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentati

No need to re-review — just fix and move on.\n\n**User Review Gate:**\nAfter the spec review loop passes, ask the user to review the written spec before proceeding:\n\n> \"Spec written and committed to `<path>`. Please review it and let me know if you want to make any changes before we start writing out the implementation plan.\"\n\nWait for the user's response. If they request changes, make them and re-run the spec review loop. Only proceed once the user approves.\n\n**Implementation:**\n\n- Invoke the writing-plans skill to create a detailed implementation plan\n- Do NOT invoke any other skill. writing-plans is the next step.\n\n## Visual Companion\n\nA browser-based companion for showing mockups, diagrams, and visual options during brainstorming. Available as a tool — not a mode. Accepting the companion means it's available for questions that benefit from visual treatment; it does NOT mean every question goes through the browser.\n\n**Offering the companion (just-in-time):** Do NOT offer it upfront. Wait until a question would genuinely be clearer shown than told — a real mockup / layout / diagram question, not merely a UI *topic*. The first time that happens, offer it then, as its own message:\n> \"This next part might be easier if I show you — I can put together mockups, diagrams, and comparisons in a browser tab as we go. It's still new and can be token-intensive. Want me to? I'll open it for you.\"\n\n**This offer MUST be its own message.** Only the offer — no clarifying question, summary, or other content. The test: **would the user understand this better by seeing it than reading it?**\n\n- **Use the browser** for content that IS visual — mockups, wireframes, layout comparisons, architecture diagrams, side-by-side visual designs\n- **Use the terminal** for content that is text — requirements questions, conceptual choices, tradeoff lists, A/B/C/D text options, scope decisions\n\nA question about a UI topic is not automatically a visual question. \"What does personality mean in this context?\" is a conceptual question — use the terminal. \"Which wizard layout works better?\" is a visual question — use the browser.\n\nIf they agree to the companion, read the detailed guide before proceeding:\n`skills/brainstorming/visual-companion.md`\n# Writing Good Tests\n\n**Load this reference when:** writing or changing tests, adding mocks, or\nadding cleanup/helper methods for tests.\n\n## Overview\n\nA test exists to catch a specific break. Two principles govern everything\nhere:\n\n```\n1. Every test names the break it catches\n2. Every test exercises the real thing\n```\n\nStrict TDD produces both naturally: a test written first and watched\nfailing against real code has already proven it can fail, and only earns\na mock when the real dependency proves slow or external.\n\n## Principle 1: Name the Break\n\nBefore writing the test body, answer: **what production change should\nmake this test fail — and is that change a bug or a decision?** A test\nearns its place by catching a wrong branch, missing side effect, wrong\nargument, boundary case, or broken contract.\n\n**Derive expectations independently.** Use literals and hand-checked\nfixtures; table-driven tests with literal `want` values are the preferred\nshape. An expectation computed by the code under test — or its helpers —\npasses no matter what that code does:\n\n```typescript\n// ❌ Mirror assertion: the same builder computes both sides — always true\nconst expected = buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' });\nexpect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe(expected);\n\n// ✅ Hand-derived literal\nexpect(buildSearchQuery({ tag: 'urgent' })).toBe('tag:\"urgent\"');\n```\n\n**No change detectors.** If only intentional decisions can fail a test —\na constant's value, exact message wording, private structure — it fires\non redesign and sleeps through bugs. Test the behavior that depends on\nthe decision: not `expect(MAX_RETRIES).toBe(5)` but \"a failing call is\nretried 5 times and the 6th attempt never happens.\"\n\n**Behavior, not text.** Asserting that a script, skill, or config\ncontains an exact line proves only that the source is the source. Run\nscripts against controlled inputs and assert outputs, side effects, or\nexit codes. Documents that instruct agents are tested by the consuming\nagent's behavior (superpowers:writing-skills); prose for humans earns no\ntest at all.\n\n**Your code, not the framework.** Test the contract your code makes at\nits boundaries — the route you register, the query you emit, the payload\nyou produce. Upstream mechanics are their maintainers' tests to write\n(the classic: asserting your router invokes a registered handler — that\nis the framework's test, not yours). When upstream behavior genuinely\nsurprised you, write one narrow characterization test naming the\nassumption. The same boundary applies inside your code: constructors,\ngetters, constants, and trivial forwarding earn tests only when they\nvalidate, normalize, default, derive, enforce, or cause side effects —\notherwise assert the first consumer-visible result that depends on them.\n\n### Gate Function\n\n```\nBEFORE writing the test body:\n  Name the production change that would make this test fail.\n\n  Cannot name one            → redesign around an observable behavior\n  \"The source text changed\"  → run the artifact and assert its effects\n  Only intentional decisions → change detector; test the behavior\n                               that depends on the decision\n\n  Confirm the expected value is derived without the code under test.\n  IF it reuses the code's logic or helpers:\n    Replace it with a literal or hand-checked fixture\n```\n\n## Principle 2: Exercise the Real Thing\n\n**The mock earns no assertions.** A mock assertion passes when the mock\nis present and fails when it is absent — it says nothing about the\ncomponent. Assert the real component's behavior; if the mock is what you\nare checking, unmock it or delete the assertion.\n\n```typescript\n// ✅ Real behavior\nexpect(screen.getByRole('navigation')).toBeInTheDocument();\n\n// ❌ Mock existence\nexpect(screen.getByTestId('sidebar-mock')).toBeInTheDocument();\n```\n\n**your human partner's correction:** \"Are we testing the behavior of a\nmock?\"\n\n**Mock at the right level.** Learn every side effect of the real method\nbefore replacing it; mock the slow or external operation and keep what\nthe test depends on real. When unsure, run the test against the real\nimplementation first and observe what actually needs to happen.\n\n```typescript\n// ❌ The mock swallows the config write that duplicate detection reads\nvi.mock('ToolCatalog', () => ({\n  discoverAndCacheTools: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined)\n}));\n\n// ✅ Mock only the slow server startup; the config write stays real\nvi.mock('MCPServerManager');\n```\n\n**Make doubles specific.** When arguments, call counts, or ordering are\npart of the contract, assert them — a fake that accepts anything verifies\nnothing. Give each branch (success, error, malformed) its own fixture or\nspy, so the wrong branch cannot satisfy the expectation.\n\n**Mirror real data completely.** Mock the complete structure as it exists\nin reality — all documented fields — not just the ones your test reads.\nPartial mocks fail silently when downstream code reads an omitted field:\nthe test passes while integration breaks.\n\n**Production classes carry production methods only.** Cleanup that only\ntests need lives in test utilities, never as a `destroy()` on the\nproduction class. Ask: is this method called only from tests? Does this\nclass own this resource's lifecycle? Wrong answers → test utility.\n\n**Prefer real components over complex mocks.** When mock setup outgrows\nthe test logic, mocks miss methods the real components have, or tests\nbreak when the mock changes, switch to an integration test with real\ncomponents. **your human partner's question:** \"Do we need to be using a\nmock here?\"\n\n### Gate Function\n\n```\nBEFORE adding a mock or test helper:\n  List the real method's side effects; keep the ones the test\n  depends on real — mock the slow/external level below them.\n\n  Mock responses mirror the complete real structure.\n\n  A method only tests call lives in test utilities, not production.\n\n  About to assert on the mock itself?\n    Unmock it or delete the assertion.\n```\n\n## Tests Ship With the Implementation\n\nThe TDD cycle — failing test, minimal implementation, refactor — is what\n\"complete\" means. Ship the tests the behavior needs and only those:\ntrivial code and human prose earn none, and a test written to satisfy\nprocess costs maintenance forever.\n\n## The Mutation Check\n\nBefore finishing, mentally mutate the production code; at least one test\nshould fail for each realistic mutation:\n\n- Wrong constant or argument\n- Wrong branch handler\n- Missing state change or side effect\n- Empty or default return\n- Missing validation for zero, empty, nil, unauthorized, or malformed input\n\nA mutation nothing catches marks the behavior as unprotected — or the\ntest as tautological.\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| When you... | Do |\n|-------------|-----|\n| Write any test | Name the break it catches — a bug, not a decision |\n| Build an expected value | Derive it by hand; never with the code under test |\n| Test a script or document | Run it / pressure-test its consumer; never grep its text |\n| Reach for a dependency test | Test your boundary contract, not their documented mechanics |\n| Want to assert on a mocked element | Test the real component, or unmock it |\n| Are about to mock a method | Learn its side effects; mock the slow/external level |\n| Build a mock response | Mirror the real structure completely |\n| Need cleanup only tests use | Put it in test utilities |\n| Watch mock setup balloon | Switch to an integration test with real components |\n| Finish a test file | Run the mutation check |\n\n## Warning Signs\n\n- Setup and assertion share the same object, guaranteeing equality\n- The test can fail only through a panic, crash, or missing selector\n- The test fails on every intentional change, never on accidental breakage\n- Expected values are hidden behind loops, builders, or helpers\n- The test greps source text, or asserts a removed symbol stays removed\n- The test would still matter if only the framework remained\n- The test exists for coverage, checking no side effect or outcome\n- An assertion checks a `*-mock` test ID, or fails if you remove the mock\n- A method is called only from test files\n- Mock setup is more than half the test, or you can't explain why the mock is needed\n- Mocking \"just to be safe\"\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Every one of them belongs to a temporary repository that no longer exists. Nothing in hive-mind — not `--auto-cleanup`, not `hive-cleanup`, not `disk-guard.lib.mjs` — is aware that this directory exists, so the space is never reclaimed and the disk pre-flight gate cannot see the growth coming.\\n\\nObserved on `konard/hive-mind-dind:2.15.1`, hive-mind `2.15.1`, `@link-assistant/agent` `0.26.0`.\\n\\n## Reproduction / observed run\\n\\n```\\nsolve https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/issues/1069 \\\\\\n  --think xhigh --tool codex --attach-logs --verbose \\\\\\n  --no-tool-check --disable-report-issue --language en\\n```\\n\\nContainer `a182caf61c25`, writable layer **56.5 GB** after ~9.5 h. On this host that exhausts the remaining 79 GB in well under a day.\\n\\n## Root cause\\n\\nThree things compose into an unbounded leak.\\n\\n**1. `@link-assistant/agent` keys its snapshot store on the repository's root commit.**\\n\\n`src/snapshot/index.ts`:\\n\\n```ts\\nfunction gitdir() {\\n  const project = Instance.project;\\n  return path.join(Global.Path.data, 'snapshot', project.id);\\n}\\n```\\n\\nand `src/project/project.ts` derives that id from the first root commit:\\n\\n```ts\\nconst roots = await $`git rev-list --max-parents=0 --all`...\\nid = roots[0];\\n```\\n\\n`Snapshot.track()` then does `git init` into that directory and `git add .` over the whole worktree.\\n\\n**2. The workload runs the agent inside throwaway repositories created with a fresh `git init`.**\\n\\n`experiments/issue_1028_agent_cli_ladder/run.sh` in the target repo, once per ladder node:\\n\\n```sh\\nwork=$(mktemp -d)\\ngit -C \\\"$ROOT\\\" archive HEAD | tar -x -C \\\"$work\\\"\\ngit -C \\\"$work\\\" init -q\\ngit -C \\\"$work\\\" commit -qm ladder-fixture     # ← brand-new root commit every time\\n\\\"$AGENT\\\" --no-summarize-session ...\\n```\\n\\nEach `git init` + commit produces a **unique** root-commit hash, so every invocation looks to the agent like a brand-new project and gets its own `snapshot/<id>/` — containing a full copy of the ~270 MB worktree. The stores share nothing: I checked, **zero** of the 115 have an `objects/info/alternates`.\\n\\nThe storage sidecar confirms the 1:1 mapping — 116 entries under `storage/project/`, each pointing at a dead temp dir:\\n\\n```json\\n{ \\\"id\\\": \\\"00afb1665ac7a67df77158fdef92cbc1f77f68c8\\\",\\n  \\\"worktree\\\": \\\"/tmp/tmp.AqWrQDVV2c\\\", \\\"vcs\\\": \\\"git\\\", ... }\\n```\\n\\n**3. `$XDG_DATA_HOME` is outside the workspace, so every cleanup path misses it.**\\n\\n`run.sh` *does* clean up correctly — `trap cleanup_one RETURN` removes `$work`. But the snapshot store lives in `~/.local/share/`, not under `$work`, so removing the worktree orphans its snapshot permanently. And on the hive-mind side:\\n\\n- `disk-guard.lib.mjs` — `SOLVER_WORKSPACE_PREFIX = 'gh-issue-solver-'`, `listSolverWorkspaces()` scans only `/tmp`.\\n- `cleanup.lib.mjs` — `HIVE_MIND_TEMP_PATTERNS` is 15 basename regexes, all rooted at `/tmp` / `/var/tmp`. Nothing matches a home directory.\\n- `listCleanableTempEntries()` — `roots = ['/tmp', '/var/tmp']`.\\n- `cleanupTempDirectory()` (`solve.repository.lib.mjs:1318`) removes `tempDir` only.\\n\\n`grep -rn \\\"XDG_DATA_HOME\\\\|\\\\.local/share\\\\|getDataHome\\\" src/` returns **nothing**. Agent state under `~/.local/share/` and `~/.codex/` is simply not part of hive-mind's disk model.\\n\\n## Why this is hive-mind's to fix\\n\\nhive-mind ships `@link-assistant/agent` in its own image (`Dockerfile:179`, `Dockerfile.dind:187`), exposes it as `--tool agent`, and owns the disk accounting for the container: the 10 GB pre-flight gate, `disk-guard.lib.mjs`, and `hive-cleanup`. Right now all three measure only `/tmp`, so a task can consume 31 GB of home-directory state while every hive-mind disk check reports a healthy workspace. That is exactly the failure mode #2160 was meant to prevent, one directory over.\\n\\nIt also compounds a second, already-known behaviour: the target repo is public, so `argv.autoCleanup` resolved to `false` (`solve.mjs:280-286`) and the 16 GB `/tmp/gh-issue-solver-*` workspace is kept too.\\n\\n## Proposed fix\\n\\n**A. Reclaim agent state when a task finishes successfully** — the ask that started this report.\\n\\nExtend `cleanupTempDirectory()` (or a new `cleanupAgentState()` called from the same place) so that when cleanup runs, it also prunes agent-side state whose worktree no longer exists:\\n\\n```js\\n// ~/.local/share/link-assistant-agent/snapshot/<projectId>\\n// ~/.local/share/link-assistant-agent/storage/{project,session,message,part,session_diff}/<id>\\n```\\n\\nSafe pruning rule, cheap to implement: for each `storage/project/<id>.json`, read `worktree`; if that path no longer exists on disk, the project is dead — delete its `snapshot/<id>/` and its storage records. That is precisely the 115 orphans here and cannot touch a live session. Snapshots with no project record and an mtime older than the idle threshold should also go.\\n\\n**B. Make it unconditional on success, not gated on `--auto-cleanup`.**\\n\\nOrphaned snapshots have no debugging value once their worktree is gone — there is nothing left to restore them into.                      |\n+\n+## Existing components and libraries considered\n+\n+### Free-space measurement\n+\n+| Option                                                                                                                                                                      | Assessment                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |\n+| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n+| [`check-disk-space`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/check-disk-space) (~1.1M weekly downloads, no native deps; shells out to `df` on POSIX and `wmic`/PowerShell on Windows) | Closest match to what the guard needs. Rejected for now because Hive Mind resolves dependencies at runtime through use-m and the guard must work when nothing can be fetched; the single `df -Pk` call is ~10 lines and is the same mechanism the library uses internally on Linux, which is the only platform the DinD image targets. |\n+| [`diskusage`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/diskusage) (native `statvfs`/`GetDiskFreeSpaceEx`)                                                                              | Most accurate and avoids parsing text, but a native addon in a runtime-resolved dependency chain is a build risk inside the container for a value used once per task.                                                                                                                                                                  |\n+| [`node-disk-info`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/node-disk-info)                                                                                                            | Enumerates all filesystems; more than needed, and the parsing surface is larger than `df -Pk`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |\n+| `fs.statfs` (Node ≥ 18.15)                                                                                                                                                  | Attractive: no dependency, no parsing. Worth migrating to — tracked as follow-up F1 below. The run's Node v24.3.0 supports it.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |\n+\n+`df -Pk` was chosen deliberately: `-P` guarantees POSIX single-line-per-filesystem output, which is\n+what makes the parse safe against long device names that otherwise wrap.\n+\n+### Temp-directory reclamation\n+\n+- **systemd-tmpfiles** ageing (`10d` for `/tmp`, `30d` for `/var/tmp`, per systemd.io's _Using /tmp/\n+  and /var/tmp/ Safely_) is the standard answer for host-level cleanup, but its time-based policy is\n+  far too slow for a run that fills 65 GB in four hours, and it is not available inside every\n+  container.\n+- The known incidents where tmpfiles ageing deleted _in-use_ files\n+  ([NixOS/nixpkgs#86600](https://github.com/NixOS/nixpkgs/issues/86600), Ubuntu\n+  [LP#2088268](https://bugs.launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/systemd/+bug/2088268)) are the reason the\n+  guard is built on \"enumerate, then never touch anything busy\" rather than on age alone: a\n+  long-running solve session can leave a workspace untouched for hours and still need it.\n+- **tmpreaper** has the same age-based model and the same blind spot, plus it is Debian-specific.\n+- `/proc/<pid>/cwd` scanning is what `lsof`/`fuser` do for the cwd case, without requiring either\n+  binary in the image. `fuser -m` would additionally catch open file handles outside the cwd; the\n+  cwd signal is sufficient here because the AI tool runs _in_ its workspace, and adding open-handle\n+  detection is follow-up F2.\n+\n+### Exit-code semantics\n+\n+`EX_TEMPFAIL = 75` comes from `sysexits.h` and is documented as \"temporary failure, indicating\n+something that is not really an error … the request should be reattempted later\"\n+([sysexits(3)](https://man.netbsd.org/sysexits.3),\n+[man7.org sysexits.h](https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/sysexits.h.3head.html)). Reusing it\n+rather than inventing a code means existing supervisors and CI retry policies interpret hive's\n+\"blocked, not broken\" outcome correctly with no extra configuration.\n+\n+### Queue-level backpressure\n+\n+The deferral mechanism added here is a hand-rolled admission control. Established alternatives\n+(`p-queue` concurrency/interval limits, `bottleneck` reservoirs) throttle by _rate_, not by an\n+external resource that in-flight work releases, so neither expresses \"hold this task until a peer\n+frees 10 GB\". The requeue-with-deferral-counter approach also preserves the existing `IssueQueue`\n+semantics (`queue`/`processing`/`completed`/`failed` + `deferrals`), which is why it was preferred\n+over replacing the queue.\n+\n+## Remaining risk and follow-ups\n+\n+| ID  | Item                                                                                                                     | Rationale                                                                                                                                                                                  |\n+| --- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |\n+| F1  | Replace the `df -Pk` child process with `fs.statfs`                                                                      | Removes text parsing and a process spawn per task; keep `df` as fallback for older runtimes                                                                                                |\n+| F2  | Extend busy detection to open file handles (`/proc/<pid>/fd`), not just cwd                                              | A worker holding a log file open in a workspace it is not sitting in is currently only protected by `protectedPaths`                                                                       |\n+| F3  | Decide whether `--auto-cleanup` should default _on_ for orchestrated runs                                                | The public-repository default is what filled the disk. The safe cleanup from P7 makes on-by-default defensible, but changing a default is a behaviour change and belongs in its own change |\n+| F4  | Report disk-blocked tasks in the final summary as a distinct line (`⏸️ N deferred`) rather than only in the exit message | Makes the outcome legible without reading the exit code                                                                                                                                    |\n+| F5  | Emit the marginal disk cost per completed task                                                                           | 10.8 GB/task was derived by arithmetic here; measuring it directly would let hive predict how many tasks a host can run                                                                    |\n+\n+Note on scope: F1–F5 are deliberately **not** in PR #2162. Each is an enhancement beyond \"find and\n+fix the causes of the reported symptoms\", and F3 in particular changes observable defaults.\n+\n+## Sources consulted\n+\n+- [sysexits(3), Nothing was wrong with the four \"failed\" issues: a follow-up run solved all four the next morning in [router PR #202](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/202).\n+\n+What actually happened is that the container ran out of disk. Each completed task left its ~10.8 GB solver workspace in `/tmp`, because `--auto-cleanup` defaults to off. Free space fell 74 938 MB → 10 047 MB over the six completed tasks. Hive checked disk space **once**, at startup, so it kept dequeuing work; each of the last four tasks then tripped `solve`'s own `--min-disk-space 10240` pre-flight check, exited `1` after ~7 seconds without ever looking at the issue, and posted a \"🚨 Solution Draft Failed\" comment on the target repository. Four environment conditions were counted as four task failures.\n+\n+The same run also mislabelled the work it _had_ completed. four task failures\n+\n+**Symptom.** `❌ 4 task(s) failed (completed: 6)`, exit 1, and four \"🚨 Solution Draft Failed /\n+Reason: System checks failed\" comments on router #192–#195.\n+\n+**Chain of causes.**\n+\n+1. `router` is a public repository, and `solve` defaults `--auto-cleanup` to off for public\n+   repositories. Each finished task therefore left its `/tmp/gh-issue-solver-*` clone in place.\n+   The run's own numbers: 74 935 → 57 507 → 42 391 → 25 673 → 18 624 → 10 047 MB free, i.e. about\n+   10.8 GB per completed task, 65 GB across six.\n+2. Hive measured free space once, in start-up validation (log line 86), and never again. The\n+   producer/consumer loop had no notion of a resource that shrinks while it dequeues.\n+3. Reaching 10 047 MB free, each of the last four tasks failed `solve`'s `--min-disk-space 10240`\n+   pre-flight check, exited `1` ~7 s after start, and reported through the _task-failure_ path —\n+   the only outcome the worker loop had besides success.\n+4. Because a worker that cannot start still had to produce an outcome, the issue was moved to\n+   `failed`, never retried, and a failure comment was published to the target repository.\n+\n+The distinguishing evidence that this is not a task problem at all: a later run solved all four\n+issues in [router PR #202](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/pull/202) (created\n+2026-08-17T04:49:33Z, merged 06:07:57Z) without any change to the issues.\n+\n+**Fix.** A new module, `src/disk-guard.lib.mjs`, gives the orchestrator a third outcome:\n+\n+- `getFreeDiskSpaceMB()` — `df -Pk` (POSIX-portable single-line output), `null` when unavailable.\n+- `listSolverWorkspaces()` — every `/tmp/gh-issue-solver-*` directory, oldest mtime first.\n+- `findBusySolverWorkspaces()` — workspaces that are some process's `/proc/<pid>/cwd`. When `/proc`\n+  cannot be read, **every** workspace is reported busy (`src/disk-guard.lib.mjs:100-121`); refusing\n+  to guess is the only safe answer when deleting would destroy live work.\n+- `reclaimSolverWorkspaces()` — removes idle workspaces oldest-first until the requirement is met,\n+  skipping in-flight (`in_flight`), busy (`process_cwd`) and recently touched (`recently_modified`,\n+  default 5 min) ones.\n+- `ensureDiskSpaceForWorker()` — reclaim, then poll while other work is in flight, then answer\n+  `{ ok: false, reason: 'insufficient_disk_space' }`.\n+\n+`src/hive.mjs` uses it per task (`src/hive.mjs:709-723`): it tracks each worker's workspaces in\n+`workerWorkspaces` and passes `getProtectedWorkspacePaths()` so a running worker's clone can never be\n+reclaimed; it waits up to `DISK_SPACE_WAIT_MS` (10 min) **only** when another worker is still\n+running (waiting when nothing can release space would just stall); and on failure it calls\n+`issueQueue.requeue(issueUrl)` and counts a deferral instead of a failure. After\n+`MAX_DISK_SPACE_DEFERRALS` (3) with nothing in flight, `diskSpaceHalt` is set and hive exits with\n+`EXIT_CODE_INSUFFICIENT_DISK_SPACE` (75 = `EX_TEMPFAIL`) and the message `… — N task(s) completed,\n+M left queued (no task failures)` (`src/hive.mjs:1412-1413`).\n+\n+`solve` now exits 75 as well when its own pre-flight check fails on disk space\n+(`src/solve.mjs:229-231`), with `skipPreExit: true` so it does not publish a \"Solution Draft Failed\"\n+comment for something the issue is not responsible for; `src/hive.mjs:875` recognises that exit code\n+and treats it as a deferral even when the worker was spawned before space ran out.\n+\n+Choosing 75 rather than a bespoke code matters for the callers of `hive` (CI, cron, supervisors):\n+sysexits defines `EX_TEMPFAIL` as \"temporary failure, indicating something that is not really an\n+error … the request should be reattempted later\", which is exactly the retry contract wanted here.\n+\n+**Test.** `tests/disk-guard-2160.test.mjs` — 15 cases with injected `df`/`readdir`/`readlink`/`rm`/\n+clock/sleep, including the reproduction of this run's exact sequence (six workspaces, 10 047 MB free,\n+requirement 10 240 MB) which asserts the task is deferred and requeued rather than failed.\n+\n+## P2 — `⚠️ Could not rename log file: getLogFile is not a function`\n+\n+`src/solve.restart-shared.lib.mjs` passed no-op `getLogFile`/`setLogFile` stubs to five tool\n+executors and omitted them entirely for `executeClaude`, so every restart/watch/auto-merge iteration\n+threw a `TypeError` inside the rename block and left the session log unnamed. Fixed by extracting the\n+logic into `src/session-log-rename.lib.mjs` — which never throws and returns\n+`{ ok: false, reason: 'missing_accessors' | 'missing_session_id' | … }` — and forwarding the real\n+accessors from `src/lib.mjs` at every call site. Test: `tests/session-log-rename-2160.test.mjs`.\n+\n+## P3 — `⚠️ WARNING: .gitkeep still exists after cleanup`\n+\n+`cleanupClaudeFile` warned first and only then checked whether the file predated the session, so a\n+`.gitkeep` that belongs to the repository produced a warning immediately followed by\n+`ℹ️ .gitkeep existed before this session — keeping pre-existing file`. The pre-existence check\n+(`git cat-file -e <commit>~1:<file>`) now runs first and the warning is emitted only for a real\n+leftover (`src/solve.results.lib.mjs:485-500`). Test:\n+`tests/gitkeep-cleanup-warning-2160.test.mjs`.\n+\n+## P4 — 26 × `⚠️ Tool result error detected`\n+\n+All 26 were the AI's own command failing _inside_ the session, after which the AI read the result and\n+continued: 11 harness-blocked `sleep`s (`Blocked: sleep 240 followed by: …`), 9 Bash timeouts\n+(`Exit code 143`, the SIGTERM of the tool's own timeout), 4 × `Exit code 1`, 2 × `Exit code 127`.\n+Two consequences: the run log looked degraded, and each such result overwrote \"the last thing the\n+assistant said\", so a truncated stream could be reported as having failed _after_\n+`Blocked: sleep 240 …` instead of after the AI's actual last message.\n+\n+`classifyToolResultError()` (`src/claude.stream-events.lib.mjs:40-51`) returns\n+`{ benign, category }` for harness blocks, command timeouts and bare exit codes; benign results are\n+logged as `ℹ️` and no longer replace `lastText`. Anything unrecognised keeps its previous treatment,\n+so the change cannot hide a new class of error.\n+\n+The benign text is still kept, in its own variable, because issue #2023 needs _something_ to name\n+when a stream ends with no terminal result event and the AI never spoke — `Exit code 144` after a\n+lone `gh run view` is exactly that case. `buildMissingClaudeResultMessage()` therefore prefers a\n+real tool error, then the last assistant message, then a benign result. That ordering is what keeps\n+both regression tests true at once: `tests/test-issue-2023-claude-missing-result-resume.mjs` still\n+reports \"after: Exit code 144\", while a blocked `sleep` never displaces something the AI said.\n+\n+Prompt guidance in all four locales now tells the AI to poll with an `until` loop instead of a long\n+foreground `sleep`, removing the most common trigger. Test:\n+`tests/tool-result-error-classification-2160.test.mjs` (17 cases, including the exact strings from\n+this run).\n+\n+## P5 — messages that described something that did not happen\n+\n+- `📁 Keeping directory (--no-auto-cleanup)` — the flag was never passed; auto-cleanup was _defaulted_\n+  off because the repository is public. The line now names the actual reason via\n+  `argv.autoCleanupSource` (`src/solve.repository.lib.mjs:1338-1346`). This is the single line that\n+  would have made P1 diagnosable from the log alone.\n+- `⚠️ Log comment too long (N chars)` (10×) — the expected route for a long log, which\n+  `gh-upload-log` then handles. Downgraded to `ℹ️` and it now names the fallback\n+  (`src/github.lib.mjs:579-584`).\n+\n+Test: `tests/misleading-messages-2160.test.mjs`.\n+\n+## P6 — six merged solution drafts reported as `(no PR found)`\n+\n+`listSolutionDrafts` called `batchCheckPullRequestsForIssues`, whose GraphQL/REST timeline walk kept\n+only pull requests in state `OPEN`. With `--auto-merge` every draft was already merged by the time\n+the summary ran, so the summary of a successful run claimed no work existed — the most misleading\n+line in the report, because a human reads it to decide whether the run was useful.\n+\n+`batchCheckPullRequestsForIssues` and `extractLinkedPullRequestsForIssue` now take\n+`includeStates` (default `['OPEN']`, so no existing caller changes behaviour) and `openPRCount`\n+still counts only open ones, which keeps `--skip-issues-with-prs` correct\n+(`src/github.batch.lib.mjs:25-35,70-74,152-198`). The listing asks for\n+`['OPEN','MERGED','CLOSED']` and prints the state for non-open drafts\n+(`src/list-solution-drafts.lib.mjs:11,38-44`). Both consumers of the batch checker were audited so\n+the fix is complete, per R6. Test: `tests/solution-draft-listing-2160.test.mjs`.\n+\n+## P7 — `--auto-cleanup` was a no-op in one branch and `rm -rf /tmp/*` in the other\n+\n+Two defects in the same feature, neither visible in this run because the flag was off:\n+\n+1. `src/hive.mjs` called `cleanupTempDirectories()` with no arguments in its non-`--once` branch,\n+   while the function begins `if (!argv || !argv.autoCleanup) return;` — a silent no-op that could\n+   never clean anything, even with `--auto-cleanup`. Fixed at `src/hive.mjs:1335`.\n+2. The cleanup ran `sudo rm -rf /tmp/* /var/tmp/*`, which also destroys the workspaces, lock\n+   directories and logs of any _concurrent_ hive/solve run on the same host — and the run doing the\n+   cleanup is rarely the only tenant of `/tmp`. In this very run two workers shared `/tmp`, so\n+   cleanup fired by worker 1 would have deleted worker 2's live clone. It now goes through\n+   `listCleanableTempEntries()` (`src/disk-guard.lib.mjs:137-169`), which enumerates entries and\n+   keeps anything a live process sits in, anything the caller protects, and the run's own log file,\n+   logging each kept entry with its reason.\n+\n+The array interpolation used for the narrowed command (`` $`sudo rm -rf ${remove}` ``) was verified\n+empirically to expand to one argv entry per path, with spaces and quotes preserved:\n+[`experiments/issue-2160-command-stream-array-probe.mjs`](../../../experiments/issue-2160-command-stream-array-probe.mjs).\n+Test: `tests/temp-cleanup-2160.test.mjs`, which also asserts by source inspection that no executed\n+command template deletes a whole temp root and that every `cleanupTempDirectories` call forwards\n+`argv`.\n+\n+## P8 — duplicate JSONL entries logged as a warning (and an upstream finding)\n+\n+`src/claude.lib.mjs` deduplicates transcript entries by `entry.message.id` before summing tokens, and\n+then warned about having done so. Ten sessions in this run skipped between 13 and 86 duplicates\n+each. The line already cited the upstream cause but was emitted as `⚠️`; since dedup has already\n+made the totals correct by the time it prints, nothing is wrong at that point. It is now `ℹ️` and\n+says so explicitly (`src/claude.budget-stats.lib.mjs:362-363`):\n+\n+```\n+ℹ️  JSONL deduplication: skipped 13 duplicate entries so token totals stay correct\n+    (known upstream behaviour: anthropics/claude-code#87303)\n+```\n+\n+The duplication itself is not a Hive Mind defect. It was reported upstream as\n+[anthropics/claude-code#6805](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/6805) (\"[BUG] Token\n+Usage Statistics Duplicated in stream-json Mode Causing Massive Cost Inflation\", opened 2025-08-29,\n+closed 2026-02-14 as inactive, locked 2026-02-21), so per that issue's own closing message a fresh\n+report was needed. Investigating it produced first-hand evidence of the mechanism:\n+\n+```\n+$ node experiments/issue-2160-claude-jsonl-usage-duplication.mjs <session>.jsonl\n+records: 521, distinctMessageIds: 323, duplicatedRecords: 198,\n+idsWithDuplicates: 188, idsWhoseDuplicatesAreIdentical: 188, maxEntriesPerMessageId: 3\n+inflation: input 1.21x, cache_creation 1.92x, cache_read 1.59x, output 1.86x\n+```\n+\n+One API response whose content has several blocks is written as one `assistant` entry **per block**\n+(`text | tool_use | tool_use`, `thinking | tool_use`, …), and each entry repeats the whole `usage`\n+object byte-identically — so a naive sum inflates by 1.2–1.9x on a tool-using session. Filed as\n+[anthropics/claude-code#87303](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/87303) with\n+reproduction, workaround (dedup by `message.id`) and two concrete fix options; the submitted text is\n+preserved in\n+[`upstream/claude-code-jsonl-usage-duplication.md`](./upstream/claude-code-jsonl-usage-duplication.md),\n+and the measurement script is\n+[`experiments/issue-2160-claude-jsonl-usage-duplication.mjs`](../../../experiments/issue-2160-claude-jsonl-usage-duplication.mjs).\n+\n+## Findings that were correct behaviour\n+\n+- **9 × `⚠️ Merge conflicts detected`** — genuine conflicts against a moving `main`; the restart loop\n+  resolves them and the affected PRs merged. No change.\n+- **2 × `❌ CI/CD checks are failing`** — real failures in the target repository's checks, which is\n+  what that message is for. No change.\n+- **10 × `⚠️ Security warning: --attach-logs`** — the operator passed `--attach-logs`; warning once\n+  per task is intentional. No change.\n+- **`❌ {error}`** — a literal line inside a Rust source snippet in a tool-result payload, not Hive\n+  Mind output. No change.\n+\n+## Diagnostics added (R4)\n+\n+Insufficient data was the reason P1 needed reconstruction from disk arithmetic rather than being\n+readable in the log. `process_cwd`, `recently_modified`,\n+  `remove_failed`) and the space recovered;\n+- each deferral with its counter (`deferral N/3, not a task failure`) and, on halt, how many tasks\n+  completed and how many remain queued;\n+- the real reason a workspace is being kept (`auto-cleanup is off by default for public\n+repositories`), which is what makes the disk growth self-explanatory next time;\n+- \"main\",\n+  \"body\": \"Closes #187 partially — see \\\"Not included\\\" below.\\n\\n## What was broken\\n\\n1. **The native Gemini namespace routed by provider, not by model.** `/api/gemini/v1beta/*` only worked under `UPSTREAM_PROVIDER=gemini`, so with a healthy Codex subscription `GET /api/gemini/v1beta/models` returned `{\\\"models\\\":[]}` while `/v1/models`, `/api/openai/v1/models`, `/api/codex/v1/models`, `/api/anthropic/v1/models` and `/api/qwen/v1/models` all returned the same 8 live models, and `…/gpt-5.4-mini:generateContent` returned `400 no healthy gemini credential is available`.\\n2. **A request could hang forever.** An Anthropic `POST /v1/messages` to a Codex model carrying only `{\\\"type\\\":\\\"web_search_20250305\\\",\\\"name\\\":\\\"web_search\\\",\\\"max_uses\\\":1}` with `tool_choice: {\\\"type\\\":\\\"any\\\"}` returned nothing for 80+ seconds.\\n\\n## Root causes and fixes\\n\\n**Gemini namespace.** The handlers resolved credentials from the configured upstream instead of from the requested model. They now resolve the owning subscription via `available_provider_for_model` over `healthy_providers`: Gemini-owned models keep the Code Assist path, and Codex/Claude/Qwen models are translated through `proxy::openai_chat_completions` so routing, budgets, auditing, metrics and capability gating stay in one place. The model list is the live catalog union, so a disconnected provider contributes nothing — no model is ever synthesized.\\n\\n**The hang has two independent causes, both fixed.**\\n\\n- `tool_choice: any`/`required` demands a *function* call, but a server-side tool is executed by the backend and never surfaces as one. A request offering only server tools leaves the upstream with no way to comply. It is now refused with a fast `400` on the Anthropic, Chat Completions and Responses surfaces (`capabilities::unhonourable_server_tool_request`), before reaching the vendor.\\n- The shared upstream `reqwest` client had **no timeout at all**. It now carries a 120 s *read* timeout (`UPSTREAM_READ_TIMEOUT_SECS`, `0` disables) — a per-read bound, so a legitimately long agentic stream stays legal while a silent backend errors out instead of hanging.\\n\\n## Tests\\n\\n- `tests/gemini_namespace_test.rs` — 8 new end-to-end tests over a stub vendor: list equals the `/v1/models` union; disconnected subscriptions are omitted; model metadata resolves and unknown models 404 in the Gemini error shape; `generateContent` serves both Codex and Claude models; `streamGenerateContent` emits Gemini SSE cross-provider; a full client tool-call/result loop completes over Codex; an unavailable model reports in the Gemini envelope; `generationConfig.maxOutputTokens` is honoured on both a Codex- and a Claude-owned model, leaving a fitting answer intact with `finishReason: \\\"STOP\\\"` and truncating an over-budget one with `finishReason: \\\"MAX_TOKENS\\\"`.\\n  **Reproduction verified**: with `src/gemini.rs` reverted, all 8 fail, including the exact reported `no healthy gemini credential is available`.\\n- `tests/router_e2e/cases_regressions.rs::a_forced_call_on_server_tools_only_fails_fast_on_every_surface` — the reported request on all three input protocols, wrapped in `tokio::time::timeout` so the time bound is asserted, not assumed; each must answer `400` well inside 10 s and must never reach the stub.\\n- `an_uncoerced_server_tool_search_still_reaches_codex` — proves the guard narrows nothing that previously worked.\\n- Unit tests for the capability gate and for `UPSTREAM_READ_TIMEOUT_SECS` parsing.\\n\\nFull suite green; `cargo fmt` and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` clean.\\n\\n## Not included, deliberately\\n\\n- **Cursor CLI Connect-RPC adapter.** Cursor speaks an unversioned private `agent.v1`/`aiserver.v1` Connect-RPC protobuf protocol over HTTP/2, and building or verifying an adapter needs a real Cursor account and a captured protocol. It cannot be implemented honestly here, so it is left out rather than stubbed. `clients list`/`doctor` already report it as unsupported with that rationale (`src/clients.rs`), which matches reality.\\n- **Refusing `max_uses` on backends that cannot enforce it.** Implementing this broke the pre-existing test `cases_core::anthropic_web_search_translates_to_codex_without_becoming_a_client_tool`, which deliberately covers translating `max_uses: 2` to Codex. Removing tested behaviour was out of scope, so `max_uses` is still translated as before; it is a known limitation. The hang it was reported alongside is fixed by the two causes above.\\n\\n## Docs\\n\\n`docs/use-cases/cli-gemini-cli.md` no longer claims the namespace needs `UPSTREAM_PROVIDER=gemini`, and documents both how `maxOutputTokens` is honoured per provider and the forced-tool-choice refusal. `README.md` documents `UPSTREAM_READ_TIMEOUT_SECS` and the cross-provider Gemini routes. \"main\",\n+  \"body\": \"Closes #189.\\n\\n## Problem\\n\\nThe router carried two admin credential models. Startup minted an admin-scoped\\n`la_sk_` HS256 JWT, while the first-visitor claim (web, Telegram, VK) and\\n`/api/admin/rotate` produced an opaque `la_admin_…` value persisted as a\\nSHA-256 digest in `admin-claim.json` — no `sub`, no `iat`/`exp`, no `scope`, no\\nlisting, no revocation. Two consequences reported on the issue:\\n\\n- after a claim, the startup `bootstrap-admin` JWT still showed as `active` /\\n  `0 / ∞` with a Revoke button, while already answering `401` on\\n  `/api/tokens/list`;\\n- a claimed/rotated `la_admin_…` credential succeeded on `/api/tokens/list` but\\n  answered `401 invalid token` on `/v1/models` — `authenticate_client` only ever\\n  called `token_manager.validate_token`, which requires the `la_sk_` prefix.\\n\\n## Solution\\n\\nOne credential model. The claim now issues an ordinary admin-scoped `la_sk_`\\nJWT with `sub`, `iat`, `exp`, `label` and `scope=admin`.\\n\\n- **`src/admin.rs`** — `AdminClaim` holds a `TokenManager` (`with_token_manager`\\n  / `attach_token_manager`, `OnceLock` for boot ordering). The claim file stores\\n  the token *id*, never the value. The two-phase anti-bricking handshake is\\n  preserved by minting the candidate **already revoked**: it authorises nothing\\n  on any surface until `confirm` reinstates it. Confirming also calls\\n  `revoke_other_admin_tokens(keep_id)`, retiring the startup `bootstrap-admin`\\n  token by id. `rotate_with_ttl` CAS-checks the on-disk claim (digest *and* id)\\n  under the exclusive claim lock, then mints the replacement via\\n  `rotate_admin_token(previous_id, …)` — one atomic swap.\\n- **`src/token.rs`** — `reinstate_token` and `revoke_other_admin_tokens`.\\n- **`src/admin_api.rs`** — `/api/admin/bootstrap` and `/api/admin/rotate` accept\\n  an optional `{\\\"ttl_hours\\\": n}` (clamped to one year); `require_admin` now\\n  delegates to `proxy::is_admin_authorised`, so both ports run one rule.\\n- **`src/proxy.rs`** — `authenticate_client` short-circuits on an admin\\n  credential (claimed credential or constant-time `TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY`) before\\n  `validate_token`. `scope=admin` is now a superset of client access: one\\n  administrator credential manages tokens *and* reaches `/v1/models`.\\n- **Migration** — existing `la_admin_…` claims keep authorising, `doctor` prints\\n  `admin_credential_warning: WARNING legacy opaque \\\\`la_admin_\\\\` credential …`,\\n  and the first rotate converts the claim into a JWT.\\n\\n`TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY` is unchanged as an optional bootstrap/compatibility\\ncredential, and the first-claim lock stays global across web, Telegram and VK.\\n\\n### Deliberate behaviour worth a reviewer's eye\\n\\nWhen a claimed admin JWT expires or is revoked, `claimed` stays true — bootstrap\\ndoes **not** reopen, because that would be a takeover vector on an idle\\ndeployment. The operator is told through `/api/admin/status` and `doctor`.\\n\\n## Tests\\n\\nReproducing coverage first, then the fix (all green locally: 428 lib tests plus\\nevery integration suite).\\n\\n- `src/admin_tests.rs::jwt_model` — credential shape and claims, inert\\n  unconfirmed candidate, retirement of `bootstrap-admin` on confirm,\\n  administrator-chosen TTL and clamping, expiry, revocation, atomic rotation by\\n  id, restart persistence, \\\"the claim file never holds the token\\\", and legacy\\n  `la_admin_` compatibility plus rotation-into-JWT migration.\\n- `tests/admin_ui_test.rs` — the harness now runs a persistent token store and\\n  can restart: web claim yields an admin JWT (`credential_kind: \\\"jwt\\\"`), TTL\\n  choice honoured, startup `bootstrap-admin` shown revoked after a claim,\\n  credential survives a restart, rotation atomic across a restart, expired\\n  credential stops administering.\\n- `tests/chat_admin_test.rs` — a chat claim yields an admin-scoped JWT that also\\n  administers the HTTP surface, and a claim in one channel closes the other\\n  (cross-channel exclusion).\\n- `tests/router_e2e/cases_regressions.rs::an_admin_credential_both_manages_tokens_and_reaches_the_models`\\n  — the acceptance check from the issue comments: `TOKEN_ADMIN_KEY` and an\\n  admin-scoped JWT each answer `200` on both `/api/tokens/list` and\\n  `/v1/models`, and both surfaces reject the credential once revoked.\\n\\nDocs (README admin-access section, chat-bot use case) and a `changelog.d`\\nfragment are included; \"main\",\n+  \"body\": \"Fixes #190.\\n\\n## The regression\\n\\n`clients setup` mints a router token (`issue_client_token`) and writes it into a 0600 environment file, but nothing recorded *which* token it was. `ClientManager::remove` only deleted files, so the minted credential stayed `revoked=false` in the token store forever — anyone holding a copy of the environment file kept working access to the router.\\n\\nReproduce on `main`:\\n\\n```bash\\nlink-assistant-router clients setup codex\\nlink-assistant-router clients remove codex\\nlink-assistant-router tokens list   # the client-codex token is still revoked=false\\n```\\n\\n`with` and `with --global` were checked and were already correct: per-run credentials are revoked by `cleanup_run_credential`, and `--global` persists no credential of its own.\\n\\n## The fix\\n\\n- **Metadata.** `TokenManager::is…id` returns the record id alongside the JWT, and setup persists a secret-free `ManagedCredential` (`<client>.credential.json`, mode 0600) recording `source` (`minted`/`supplied`), `token_id`, `label`, `issued_at`. The token itself is never written there — only the id, which is enough to revoke and useless to an attacker. It is written *after* the environment file, so a recorded id always describes a secret that exists on disk.\\n- **Atomic removal.** `clients remove` revokes first and deletes second. Deleting first would leave a live credential nobody can name any more, which is the regression itself.\\n- **User-supplied tokens are not revoked** unless `--revoke-supplied` is passed; the same token is often shared with other machines. If `--revoke-supplied` is given for a token this router cannot recognise, the command errors rather than silently doing nothing.\\n- **Fails closed.** When revocation fails, the credential file stays in place, the command prints the token id plus `tokens revoke <ID>` recovery instructions, and exits 1 — it never reports successful removal. `--force` is the documented escape hatch.\\n\\n## Tests\\n\\nNew `tests/clients_token_revocation_test.rs` drives the shipped binary end to end, for every client integration that supports permanent setup (codex, claude-code, opencode, qwen-code, agent, grok-cli) and both persistent storage backends (`text`, `binary`):\\n\\n- `setup_show_remove_revokes_the_minted_token_for_every_client_and_backend` — setup → `show` reports the credential → `remove` prints `revoked managed token <ID>` → a **fresh process** runs `tokens list` and sees `revoked=true`. The new process reads the store from disk, so this is the restart-persistence check too.\\n- `a_removed_client_credential_is_rejected_by_a_live_router` — a real `serve` process accepts `POST /v1/chat/completions` with the credential before removal and answers 401/403 after it, on both backends.\\n- `supplied_tokens_survive_remove_unless_revocation_is_requested`.\\n- `failed_revocation_keeps_the_credential_and_exits_nonzero` — store made unreadable; asserts nonzero exit, recovery instructions, and that both the environment file and the metadata survive; then `--force` succeeds.\\n- `credential_metadata_never_contains_the_token` — no `la_sk_` on disk, mode 0600.\\n\\nPlus unit tests in `src/clients/credentials.rs` for the revocability rule and the disk round trip.\\n\\nFull local checks pass: `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` (clean), file-size limits, and the entire `cargo test` suite.\\n\",\n+  \"closedAt\": \"main\",\n+  \"body\": \"Fixes all four open issues and the failing `main` CI job.\\n\\n## CI: `Verify published release provenance`\\n\\nThe only failing job on `main`. `actions/attest-build-provenance` derives the SLSA source commit from the Actions context, so the predicate always names `github.sha` — the commit the run *started* from. The `chore: release vX.Y.Z` commit is created later by that same run, so no workflow change can make the attestation name it, and every published binary and SBOM failed the guard.\\n\\nThe guard now accepts the release commit **or exactly its parent**, and still rejects an artifact attesting an unrelated commit or carrying no attestation. The verify job fetches the tag so the parent is resolvable rather than silently absent (which would have quietly weakened the check).\\n\\nVerified against the real published v0.83.0 assets that failed run `31973050076`: all 8 previously-failing artifacts now pass.\\n\\n## #195 — `max_tokens` overshoot\\n\\nA hard cap was checked against already-recorded usage, but usage is only known *after* a response completes, so one large answer could push the total arbitrarily past the cap (the reported `39273/30000`).\\n\\nThe router now **reserves** each request's declared output budget at admission and settles it against the provider's reported usage afterwards. A request that cannot fit is rejected before dispatch rather than truncated mid-answer. Reserving happens inside the same locked read-modify-write that counts the request, so concurrent requests cannot overshoot together; a `ReservationGuard` releases budget on every early return, cancellation, or usage-less response; stale reservations from an unclean shutdown are cleared at startup.\\n\\nApplies to Responses, Chat Completions, Anthropic Messages, Gemini, Gonka, Crater and OpenAI-compatible providers. `tokens list` shows reserved alongside actual spend.\\n\\n**Contract change:** the e2e test that asserted the old \\\"the response that crosses a cap completes\\\" behaviour now asserts the documented contract instead. repeats `usage` per content block\n+\n+Related upstream issue: [anthropics/claude-code#6805](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/6805)\n+— \"[BUG] Token Usage Statistics Duplicated in stream-json Mode Causing Massive Cost Inflation\"\n+(opened 2025-08-29, closed 2026-02-14 as inactive/`NOT_PLANNED`, **locked** 2026-02-21).\n+\n+Because #6805 is locked, its own closing message applies: \"please file a new issue and reference this\n+one\". The text filed upstream is reproduced verbatim below.\n+\n+Local relevance: this is the cause of the ten `JSONL deduplication: skipped N
[2026-09-02T08:01:58.757Z] [STDOUT]  duplicate entries`\n+lines in run `4c1dedd8` (P8 in [../TECHNICAL_ANALYSIS.md](../TECHNICAL_ANALYSIS.md)). Hive Mind\n+already deduplicates by `message.id`, so its own token and cost totals were never inflated; only the\n+severity of the message was wrong, and that is fixed in PR #2162.\n+\n+---\n+\n+## Filed text\n+\n+**Title:** [BUG] Session transcript repeats the full `usage` object for every content block of one API\n+response (token over-counting; follow-up to #6805)\n+\n+### Summary\n+\n+One assistant API response is written to the session transcript\n+(`~/.claude/projects/<project>/<sessionId>.jsonl`) as **several** `assistant` entries — one per\n+content block (`thinking`, `text`, each `tool_use`) — and every one of those entries repeats the\n+**complete, byte-identical `usage` object** of the single underlying response. Any consumer that sums\n+`message.usage` over the transcript (or over `stream-json` output) therefore over-counts tokens and\n+any cost derived from them.\n+\n+This is the same defect as #6805, which was closed as inactive and is now locked, so this is a fresh\n+report with first-hand measurements on a current version.\n+\n+### Environment\n+\n+- Claude Code CLI **2.1.233** (also observed on **2.1.228**)\n+- Node v24.3.0, Linux (container)\n+- `--output-format stream-json --verbose`, non-interactive automation\n+\n+### Measurement (single real session)\n+\n+| Field                         | Naive sum  | Deduplicated by `message.id` | Over-count |\n+| ----------------------------- | ---------- | ---------------------------- | ---------- |\n+| `input_tokens`                | 2 252      | 1 856                        | 1.21x      |\n+| `cache_creation_input_tokens` | 1 075 420  | 560 751                      | 1.92x      |\n+| `cache_read_input_tokens`     | 39 563 813 | 24 904 077                   | 1.59x      |\n+| `output_tokens`               | 292 325    | 157 507                      | 1.86x      |\n+\n+521 usage records for 323 distinct `message.id`s → 198 duplicated records; 188 message ids had\n+duplicates and in **all 188** the duplicated `usage` objects were byte-identical. Up to 3 entries\n+shared one `message.id`.\n+\n+The duplicated entries differ only in their content block, e.g. for\n+`msg_011Ce7zpWBJMrj6gSiJAuY7o`:\n+\n+```\n+assistant uuid=70abebf3 content=[text]      usage={input_tokens:2, cache_creation_input_tokens:24896, output_tokens:244, …}\n+assistant uuid=2c277f40 content=[tool_use]  usage={input_tokens:2, cache_creation_input_tokens:24896, output_tokens:244, …}\n+assistant uuid=99c159e5 content=[tool_use]  usage={input_tokens:2, cache_creation_input_tokens:24896, output_tokens:244, …}\n+```\n+\n+Observed block shapes behind duplicates: `text | tool_use | tool_use`, `thinking | tool_use`,\n+`thinking | tool_use | tool_use`, `thinking | text | tool_use`, `tool_use | tool_use` — i.e. it\n+happens whenever a response contains more than one content block, which for tool-using sessions is\n+most responses. Over a larger sample (10 automated sessions in one 4-hour run) every session was\n+affected, with 13, 19, 38, 39, 50, 54, 58, 63, 77 and 86 duplicated records respectively.\n+\n+### Reproduction\n+\n+```bash\n+# 1. Run any session that uses tools (so responses have several content blocks):\n+claude -p \"list the files in this repo and summarise each in one line\" \\\n+  --output-format stream-json --verbose\n+\n+# 2. Analyse that session's transcript:\n+node analyze.mjs ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<sessionId>.jsonl\n+```\n+\n+`analyze.mjs`:\n+\n+```js\n+import { readFileSync } from 'node:fs';\n+const FIELDS = ['input_tokens', 'cache_creation_input_tokens', 'cache_read_input_tokens', 'output_tokens'];\n+const seen = new Set();\n+let records = 0;\n+const naive = {},\n+  deduped = {};\n+for (const f of FIELDS) ((naive[f] = 0), (deduped[f] = 0));\n+for (const line of readFileSync(process.argv[2], 'utf8').split('\\n')) {\n+  if (!line.trim()) continue;\n+  let e;\n+  try {\n+    e = JSON.parse(line);\n+  } catch {\n+    continue;\n+  }\n+  if (!e.message?.usage || !e.message?.id) continue;\n+  records++;\n+  for (const f of FIELDS) naive[f] += e.message.usage[f] || 0;\n+  if (seen.has(e.message.id)) continue;\n+  seen.add(e.message.id);\n+  for (const f of FIELDS) deduped[f] += e.message.usage[f] || 0;\n+}\n+console.log({ records, distinct: seen.size, duplicated: records - seen.size, naive, deduped });\n+```\n+\n+Any output with `duplicated > 0` reproduces the bug. A solve\n * command typically takes the URL as its first positional argument, but we scan\n * the whole string to be tolerant of flag ordering.\n *\n * @param {string} command\n * @returns {Array<{owner: string, repo: string, type: 'issue'|'pull', number: number}>}\n */\nexport function extractTaskRefsFromCommand(command) {\n  if (!command || typeof command !== 'string') return [];\n  const refs = [];\n  const seen = new Set();\n  const re = /github\\.com[/:]([^/\\s]+)\\/([^/\\s#]+?)(?:\\.git)?\\/(issues|issue|pull|pulls)\\/(\\d+)/gi;\n  let m;\n  while ((m = re.exec(command)) !== null) {\n    const ref = parseTaskUrl(m[0]);\n    if (!ref) continue;\n    const key = `${ref.owner}/${ref.repo}#${ref.number}:${ref.type}`;\n    if (seen.has(key)) continue;\n    seen.add(key);\n    refs.push(ref);\n  }\n  return refs;\n}\n\n/**\n * Normalise an owner/repo pair extracted from a git remote URL.\n *\n * @param {string} remoteUrl\n * @returns {{owner: string, repo: string}|null}\n */\nexport function parseRemoteUrl(remoteUrl) {\n  if (!remoteUrl || typeof remoteUrl !== 'string') return null;\n  // git@github.com:owner/repo.git  OR  https://github.com/owner/repo(.git)\n  const sshMatch = remoteUrl.match(/^[^@]+@[^:]+:([^/]+)\\/(.+?)(?:\\.git)?$/);\n  if (sshMatch) return { owner: sshMatch[1], repo: sshMatch[2] };\n  const httpMatch = remoteUrl.match(/^[a-z]+:\\/\\/[^/]+\\/([^/]+)\\/(.+?)(?:\\.git)?$/i);\n  if (httpMatch) return { owner: httpMatch[1], repo: httpMatch[2] };\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction sameRepo(a, b) {\n  if (!a || !b) return false;\n  return a.owner.toLowerCase() === b.owner.toLowerCase() && a.repo.toLowerCase() === b.repo.toLowerCase();\n}\n\n/**\n * Build the set of \"active task matchers\" from the running session task list.\n * For PR tasks the resolved head branch is matched exactly; Exact branch match (covers PR continue-mode and any known branch).\n    if (m.branch && gitInfo.branch && gitInfo.branch === m.branch) {\n      return m;\n    }\n    // 2. issue-{number}-{hex} prefix match scoped to the same repository.\n    if (m.issueNumber != null && gitInfo.branch && isValidIssueBranchName(gitInfo.branch, m.issueNumber)) {\n      const repoMatches = remotes.length === 0 || remotes.some(r => sameRepo(r, m));\n      if (repoMatches) return m;\n    }\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction matchesAny(name, patterns) {\n  return patterns.some(p => (p.regex || p).test(name));\n}\n\n/**\n * Identify the hive-mind temp pattern a name matches, if any.\n *\n * @param {string} name\n * @returns {{name: string}|null}\n */\nexport function matchHiveMindPattern(name) {\n  return HIVE_MIND_TEMP_PATTERNS.find(p => p.regex.test(name)) || null;\n}\n\n/**\n * Pure classification of a single temp entry into keep/remove with a reason.\n *\n * Reason precedence (highest first): protected > self > active-process >\n * active-task > dirty-worktree > hive-mind-temp (remove) > all-mode (remove) >\n * unrecognized (keep).\n *\n * @param {{name: string, path: string, isDirectory: boolean}} entry\n * @param {Object} ctx\n * @param {string[]} ctx.protectedNames\n * @param {boolean} ctx.forceStartCommand\n * @param {boolean} ctx.includeSystem - absolute paths held by running processes\n * @param {Array} ctx.matchers - active task matchers\n * @param {Map<string,{branch, remotes, dirty}>} ctx.gitInfoByPath\n * @returns {{action: 'keep'|'remove', reason: string}}\n */\nexport function classifyEntry(entry, ctx) {\n  const { protectedNames = DEFAULT_PROTECTED_NAMES, forceStartCommand = false, includeSystem = false, includeAll = false, keepDirty = true, selfPaths = new Set(), heldPaths = new Set(), matchers = [], gitInfoByPath = new Map() } = ctx || {};\n\n  const name = entry.name;\n\n  // 1. Protected names (start-command can be forced).\n  const isStartCommand = name === 'start-command';\n  if (protectedNames.includes(name)) {\n    if (isStartCommand && forceStartCommand) {\n      // fall through to deletion logic below\n    } else {\n      return { action: 'keep', reason: 'protected' };\n    }\n  }\n\n  // 1b. System-owned entries are protected unless explicitly included.\n  if (!includeSystem && matchesAny(name, SYSTEM_PROTECTED_PATTERNS)) {\n    return { action: 'keep', reason: 'system-protected' };\n  }\n\n  // 2. Paths the cleanup process itself depends on (its own clone / cwd).\n  if (selfPaths.has(entry.path)) {\n    return { action: 'keep', reason: 'self' };\n  }\n\n  // 3. Held open / used as cwd by a running process.\n  if (heldPaths.has(entry.path)) {\n    return { action: 'keep', reason: 'active-process' };\n  }\n\n  // 4.
